— Emergencies, Crashes, Law Enforcement","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Emergencies, Crashes, Law Enforcement

FACT_ID: sec17-F01 | anchor: A01
Emergencies find even careful drivers, so readiness decides outcomes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F02 | anchor: A01
Blow a tire and clamp the wheel straight, coast off the gas with feathered brakes, and flee the roadway to safety [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F03 | anchor: A01
Front blowouts yank toward the flat, so resist overcorrection, re-straighten, and ease onto the right shoulder fast [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F04 | anchor: A01
Dead headlights get switch retries, high-beam trials, flashers or fog lamps, and a quick roadside exit [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F05 | anchor: A01
Stalled engines keep heavy-but-working steering and brakes, so muscle off the road with hard pedal pressure [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F06 | anchor: A01
Runaway throttles want eyes forward, a snap to neutral, a safe pull-off, and engine shutdown after stopping [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F07 | anchor: A01
Never yank keys or let riders grab them rolling, since locked wheels crash cars [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F08 | anchor: A01
Dead pedals get pumping first, then slow parking-brake drags released at any skid [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F09 | anchor: A01
Still rolling, downshift to a safe off-road halt and park brakeless cars for good [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F10 | anchor: A02
Crash triage starts with everybody's safety [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-F11 | anchor: A02
First clear lanes if possible, shutting the car down and still [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-F12 | anchor: A02
Then phone 911 with injuries, location, and details [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-F13 | anchor: A02
State law reports injury, death, or damage past $1,500, and missing the 72-hour window costs privileges plus penalties [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-F14 | anchor: A02
Hand officers insurance, registration, and license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-F15 | anchor: A02
Finally brief your insurer on liability and at-fault obligations to others [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec17-F16 | anchor: A03
Meet officers calm and obedient [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-F17 | anchor: A03
Autism and deaf indicators on licenses and police screens prime officers for smoother stops [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-F18 | anchor: A03
Signaled stops pull clear of lanes when safe, favoring lots or side streets on busy roads [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec17-F19 | anchor: A03
Then kill the engine, show hands on the wheel, stay calm, and obey [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ia-c:iowa-department-of-transportation-iowa-d:handbook:pdf-0064]

Misconceptions: stalled cars lose all steering and brakes, yet both still work with muscle; brake failure means coasting helplessly, yet pumping, parking brake, and gears remain; minor crashes need no report, yet injury and damage thresholds compel one.

Mnemonic: flat straight and off, dark flash and off, stall grip and off, stuck neutral and off; clear, call, show, tell.

Glossary: steer-it-clear-it (the duty to clear operable cars from lanes); blowout (a sudden tire rupture); parking brake (a manual rear-wheel brake); traffic stop (an officer-ordered pullover).

Dynamic facts: none in these pages; every emergency, crash, and enforcement rule above is stable handbook knowledge with no date-variable or place-variable values.
